sources.text:
Sen. Chris Coons (D-DE) has won reelection in the state of Delaware, beating Republican challenger Michael Katz.

With 94 percent of votes counted, Coons is winning 64.2 percent against Katz’s 35.8 percent, according to the *Washington Post* late on Tuesday evening.

For months, Coons has attacked President Donald Trump’s military operation in Iran, calling it a “war of choice” and claiming the conflict has forced prices up on Americans.

“Trump’s war of choice with Iran has catapulted us into instability and violence in the Middle East, and has also caused costs to go up for the average American, and there’s no clear end in sight,” Coons told CNN.

In another interview from April, Coons suggested that he would work to block funding for the military operation in Iran.

“I’m the senior Democrat on defense appropriations, and I won’t provide a backdoor authorization for the war through a defense supplemental,” Coons told MS NOW.

*John Binder is a reporter for Breitbart News. Email him at jbinder@breitbart.com.*

# 2026 midterm elections: Live fact-checks as Democrats flip key Senate, House seats

Democrats Abdul El-Sayed, left, James Talarico, center, and Troy Jackson, right, won key seats to control the U.S. Senate in the 2026 midterm elections. (AP photos)

By

PolitiFact Staff 
  

November 3, 2026

During the 2026 midterm elections, Democrats have won a majority in the U.S. Senate, according to media outlet projections.

Republicans entered Election Day with a 53-47 lead in the Senate. But Democrats flipped seats in Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina, Iowa, Kansas and Texas all before midnight EST; by early Wednesday morning, they had flipped a longheld Republican Senate seat in Maine and secured another in Michigan. 

PolitiFact has been covering key races and fact-checking claims about the candidates and voting. Follow this live blog for our latest updates.
